name: What makes a strong birth injury case?

mainEntity.name: What makes a strong birth injury case?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong birth injury case typically requires clear evidence of medical negligence. This means demonstrating that a healthcare provider (doctor, nurse, hospital) failed to meet the accepted standard of care during pregnancy, labor, or delivery, and this failure directly caused your child's injury. Key elements include detailed medical records, expert medical testimony supporting the breach of care and causation, and evidence of significant damages. A credible and consistent narrative of events from the parents also strengthens the case, emphasizing the impact on the child and family.
acceptedAnswer.description: A strong case requires clear evidence of medical negligence, showing a healthcare provider's failure to meet the standard of care caused the injury, supported by medical records and expert testimony.
